input.rationale:
The property named — whether the monthly on-load test was actually carried out (and shown to pick up ventilation load) in each of the last two months — is the correct property. This is a case where the act itself is the required control: a standby generator's readiness for a life-critical contingency (shed ventilation with birds lost within minutes on a warm day) depends on it having actually been run up on load and demonstrated to work, not merely on indirect signals (fuel present, panel in AUTO, battery indicator green) which are consistent with either an operable or an inoperable unit under real load. Knowing with certainty that the test was performed and passed would answer the safety question (generator may be relied on); knowing it was not performed would answer it the other way (do not rely on it). The two branches are genuinely adverse/satisfactory and do not smuggle in an absence-as-adverse improperly — here, absence of the test IS the substantive fact that would make reliance unsafe, since indirect indicators don't establish the generator actually picks up full ventilation load. The "meanwhile" action (not relying on the generator as contingency while unresolved) is the appropriate holding position and does not presume either branch.

The question bound to the fact ("Was the monthly on-load test carried out in each of the last two months, even though the log has no entry?") asks the exact fact needed: it covers both months, asks about actual performance (not just log presence), and an affirmative answer would need to include that the generator "ran up correctly" as branch A states, which a person answering honestly about whether the test was "carried out" would naturally address (carrying out an on-load test inherently entails observing the result). This is close enough to reach the property: it does not offer a weak "or" branch that could be satisfied without establishing the operability point. I find no separate ungoverned fact whose answer would independently change today's action — no additional nomination is warranted.

input.rationale:
The property named — whether the weekly calibration checks were actually carried out in the last two weeks — is the right property: it is an act (the calibration having been performed and verified against the hand kit), and knowing whether it happened does answer the safety question of whether the sensor reading can be trusted for today's session. The branches and consequent actions are sound (an absence-shaped branchB is legitimate here because the substantive adverse state IS the absence of the calibration check itself, not merely absence of documentation of some independently-true condition).

However, the question the first pass bound to this fact — 'What does a hand test of the pool water read for free chlorine and pH right now, against the operating range for the session?' — does not settle this property. That question asks for a fresh, present-moment hand test reading. Even a perfect answer to it (chlorine and pH both in range right now) would not establish that the sensor was calibrated against the hand kit in the last two weeks; it only tells you the water is currently fine by the hand kit's own measurement, which is a different fact (current water chemistry) from whether the calibration/verification procedure was performed as required. Conversely, if the log were verified as completed in both weeks, that would settle the fact directly without needing a fresh hand test at all. The two are related but distinct: one is about the sensor's calibration history, the other is about today's water chemistry as measured directly by a different method. A person could truthfully answer the bound question (report a satisfactory current hand-test reading) while the calibration checks in the past two weeks still never happened.

I am replacing/adding a clarification that directly reaches the calibration property: asking whether the weekly calibration checks were performed and recorded during the technician's absence, or whether someone can immediately perform and document the overdue calibration checks now, before opening.

I did not nominate any additional fact — the observation does not support a further decision-changing unresolved fact beyond calibration status and current water chemistry, both of which are now covered.

A blank log during a staff absence is consistent both with the checks having been done but not logged, and with them never having been done at all — these lead to different actions (open on the panel reading vs. hold the pool closed until calibration is performed). The current-conditions hand test the first pass asked for does not resolve this because it measures today's water chemistry, not whether the calibration procedure was actually performed.
proposedClarification.evidenceGap: No record confirms whether the weekly sensor-to-hand-kit calibration check occurred in either of the last two weeks, and a fresh single-point hand test does not establish a calibration history.

input.rationale: The exposure fact (FP.EXPOSURE.OBS-K4.176-308.1) is the right property, correctly framed, and is already reached by the bound question about current-speed personal dust sampling against the exposure limit — that question is sound and I leave it as VERIFIED for that fact. However, the first pass raised no hazard candidate at all and asked no question about the baler interlock, despite the observation stating that the interlocked gate was struck, rehung by a fitter, and 'nobody on shift saw whether the interlock switch was reconnected' — while the baler is running now. This is a classic case of a control that cannot be seen not being a control that was checked: the gate closes and latches (a separate, visible property) but the interlock switch's electrical/functional reconnection is a distinct, unverified property. If the interlock is reconnected and functional, the baler may continue operating as normal. If it is not reconnected, the ram chamber gate provides no interlock protection against the ram cycling while the gate is open, which is a life-critical crush hazard requiring the baler be stopped/locked out until verified. These two answers lead to materially different actions today (continue running vs. stop and verify/repair), and nothing in the observation states this was checked after the strike and rehang. This is necessary now, not at a later review, because the baler is currently running with the interlock status unknown following a physical strike to the very component in question.

proposedClarification.question: Has the interlock switch on the baler ram chamber gate been tested and confirmed to correctly stop/prevent ram operation when the gate is open, following the gate being struck and rehung by the fitter, and if not has the baler been taken out of service until that is confirmed?
proposedClarification.whyItMatters: The gate was struck and rehung, and nobody on shift saw whether the interlock switch was reconnected; the gate closing and latching is a separate, visible property from the interlock circuit being live and functional. If the interlock is not functional, the ram could cycle with the gate open, a crush hazard, while the baler is currently running.
proposedClarification.evidenceGap: No functional test or verification of the interlock switch after the gate strike and repair is stated; only that the gate mechanically closes and latches.
